Physics hand-checked: ammeter — measures current, in series, made from a galvanometer with a low resistance in parallel, ideal resistance zero; voltmeter — measures potential difference, in parallel, galvanometer with a high resistance in series, ideal resistance infinite. Matches the book's four points on each side.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: Give matching pairs of points — measures, connection, how it is made, ideal resistance — one set for each meter.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ammeter
lines: 2) It is connected in series in the
3) It is a galvanometer with a low
4) An ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Series connection and low (ideally zero) resistance are the points examiners look for.
steps.why: The whole circuit current must pass through an ammeter, so it sits in series and must add almost no resistance — otherwise it would change the current it is measuring.
common_mistakes: Saying an ammeter is connected in parallel. In parallel it would short the circuit.
Saying an ideal ammeter has high resistance. It has zero resistance.

recall.must_convey: That an ammeter measures current, is connected in series, and ideally has zero resistance.

steps.memory_tip: A for ammeter, A for along the circuit: in series, near-zero resistance.

steps.label: Voltmeter
lines: 2) It is connected in parallel across
3) It is a galvanometer with a high
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Parallel connection and high (ideally infinite) resistance are the matching points.
steps.why: A voltmeter compares two points without disturbing them, so it sits across them in parallel and must draw almost no current — which needs a very high resistance.
common_mistakes: Saying a voltmeter is connected in series. In series it would stop almost all the current.
Swapping the resistances: the LOW resistance belongs to the ammeter, the HIGH one to the voltmeter.

recall.must_convey: That a voltmeter measures potential difference, is connected in parallel, and ideally has infinite resistance.

steps.memory_tip: V for voltmeter, V for across two points: in parallel, near-infinite resistance.
